all_of: a SSO login function ignores its credential arguments and authorizes using whatever token cookie is in the shared browser jar
a JSON-binding API parses the raw request body as JSON regardless of Content-Type
an SSO token cookie is HttpOnly with no SameSite attribute
a registration endpoint allows the attacker to pre-register a fixed account the bot later tries to register
any_of: a bot that visits user-supplied URLs while holding the shared cookie jar
a flag that is submitted once into a student assignment at bot startup

chain.action: win a registration race on a fixed account (e.g. student@domain) by hammering POST /api/register with your own password before the bot's startup sequence reaches its own registerUser for the same account
chain.why: owning the account makes the bot's own student login fail, so its shared token cookie stays on the account you control

chain.action: spray the bot's visit-url endpoint (here POST /submit-url) with a data:text/html URL whose form performs a text/plain cross-site JSON login to the SSO login API for your owned account
chain.why: Gin's ShouldBindJSON parses the raw body as JSON regardless of Content-Type, so a text/plain form whose input name is the JSON prefix and value is the closing brace submits a valid JSON login and overwrites the shared SSO token cookie via Set-Cookie (no SameSite)

chain.action: let the bot's loginSSO step, which ignores its credentials and authorizes using the current shared token cookie, turn the client session into your owned account
chain.why: the parameter-confusion bug means the token cookie swap is enough to hijack the OAuth flow

chain.action: when the bot submits the flag into the first assignment at startup, it now writes into your owned account; log in as that account and read GET /submission/:id as the author
chain.why: submission reads are gated on author email or teacher role, and you are now the author

first_confirming_probe.request: hammer POST /api/register for the fixed bot account with your own password and confirm it returns 200 before the bot reaches its registerUser step
first_confirming_probe.expected: the registration succeeds and your credentials work at /api/login
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the account is already registered with an unknown random password (instance already consumed)

blast_radius: a fresh instance is required; an already-running instance is permanently consumed because the flag is submitted once at startup into an account with an unknown random password

verification.evidence: flag string read from /submission/:id as the owning author on a fresh instance

reuse_when: an OAuth SSO provider has a token cookie with no SameSite and a JSON binder that ignores Content-Type
a bot shares one cookie jar across pages and has a loginSSO bug that uses the current cookie
the flag is written once at startup into a fixed account that can be race-registered
known_traps: the registration race alone is dead: if you pre-register the student but never swap the cookie, the bot authorizes as teacher and the flag is written to an unreadable teacher account
the CSRF must use enctype=text/plain with the JSON-name trick, not url-encoded form data, because the binder requires a raw JSON body
the internal nginx port the bot resolves to (1337) differs from the external mapped port; the data URL must target the internal host:port
redirect_uri validation is strict on hostname; Host header must include the external port for the port check to pass
the authorize code exchange still requires the client_secret, so you cannot exchange a stolen code yourself; the swap works because the bot does the exchange
an instance that already ran its startup is consumed: student has a random password and the flag is unreachable
